description:
Google Flights Scraper: Fares, Airlines & Times

Search Google Flights and get one row per flight option: fare, airlines, flight numbers, times, airports, stops, layovers, aircraft, legroom and CO2. One-way or round trip, economy/business/first, 1-9 adults, any currency. $2.00 per 1,000 searches.

Pricing (pay per event, billed to your Apify account): Flight search: $0.002; platform usage billed to your account.

Runs on Apify as subimpact/google-flights-scraper.

_maxChargeUsd.description: Per-run spending cap in USD (default 0.5). Passed to Apify as the run option maxTotalChargeUsd, so the run stops when it reaches this charge.
_maxChargeUsd.title: Max charge (USD)

_maxItems.description: How many dataset items to return to the model (1-1000, default 50). Truncates the response only; it does not change what the Actor collects or charges for.
_maxItems.title: Max items returned

adults.description: Number of adult passengers (1-9). Fares are the total for all adults, exactly as Google Flights shows them.
adults.title: 👥 Adults

cabin.description: Cabin class. Every option was verified against live Google Flights pages in October 2026.
cabin.title: 💺 Cabin

country.description: 2-letter Google country code, e.g. us, my, sg, gb. It sets the Google Flights market (which points of sale and fare rules are shown); the currency comes from the Currency field.
country.title: 🌍 Country (gl)

currency.description: 3-letter currency code for the prices, e.g. USD, EUR, MYR, SGD, JPY. Google converts the fare, so the numbers are Google's conversion, not an interbank rate.
currency.title: 💱 Currency

departureDate.description: Used only when Searches is empty. YYYY-MM-DD, today or later, up to 330 days ahead. Empty means about 30 days from today.
departureDate.title: 📅 Departure date (shortcut)

from.description: Used only when Searches is empty. Departure airport or city: a 3-letter code such as KUL or a city name such as Kuala Lumpur.
from.title: 🛫 From (shortcut)

language.description: 2-letter Google interface language, e.g. en, ms, de. Prices, airline names and dates follow this language.
language.title: 🗣️ Interface language (hl)

maxConcurrency.description: How many searches run at the same time (1-10). Higher is faster and more likely to get a soft rate limit from Google.
maxConcurrency.title: ⚙️ Parallel searches

maxFlightsPerSearch.description: Upper limit of flight rows taken from each search's results page (1-300). A page usually lists 20-60 options that Google has already rendered; extra options are dropped, cheapest-first, and the drop is reported.
maxFlightsPerSearch.title: 💯 Max flight options per search

maxSearches.description: Cost ceiling: at most this many searches are run (1-200). Every successful search costs $0.002, so the default 25 caps a run at $0.05. Searches above the cap are skipped and listed in RUN_SUMMARY.
maxSearches.title: 🧮 Max searches per run

nonstopOnly.description: Only show nonstop flights. Verified: Google returns just the nonstop options and the search shows the nonstop filter as applied.
nonstopOnly.title: 🚀 Nonstop only

proxyConfiguration.description: Google Flights answers direct requests from Apify's datacenter IPs, so no proxy is used by default and the run costs nothing extra. Enable Apify Proxy (or your own proxy URLs) if you run very large jobs or see empty pages; a failed proxy setup then fails the search instead of quietly going direct.
proxyConfiguration.title: 🔌 Proxy configuration

returnDate.description: Used only when Searches is empty. YYYY-MM-DD, on or after the departure date. Leave empty for a one-way search.
returnDate.title: 📅 Return date (shortcut)

searches.description: One object per search. from/to accept a 3-letter airport or city code (KUL, SIN) or a free-text city name (Kuala Lumpur). date and returnDate are YYYY-MM-DD; returnDate null or empty means one way. adults 1-9, cabin economy, business or first. When this list is empty the shortcut fields below are used instead. Leave "date" out to search about 30 days from today.
searches.title: ✈️ Searches

to.description: Used only when Searches is empty. Arrival airport or city: a 3-letter code such as SIN or a city name such as Singapore.
to.title: 🛬 To (shortcut)

name: google_flights
